question: Is the artifact published under a given tag provably the one that was built from the commit that tag points at?
trigger: A developer pushes a commit to the repository's release branch
A firmware or binary release must be traceable back to the exact commit that produced it
A previously published tag has to be re-verified without rebuilding
decision: Publish the artifact as a release under the version tag
Refuse the release and raise the version, or fix the tree, before pushing again
Roll back a partial publication when the closed-loop check does not pass
evidence: git HEAD, HEAD tree, tracked-file manifest and work-tree status captured before and after the build
The produced artifact's file name and its own PE version resource
The commit that the remote tag resolves to, read at verification time
The SHA-256 of the release asset downloaded back from the provider
success_measure: Every published tag satisfies all three conditions at once: the tag resolves to the pushed HEAD, the artifact was built from that commit with zero tracked-file modification during the build, and the asset downloaded back from the release is byte-identical to the local artifact.
outcome: A published release whose artifact, tag and source commit are provably the same thing, or a named refusal that published nothing.
input_types: a version embedded in the artifact file name
output_artifacts: a tag and release on the configured remote
use_cases: re-verification of an already published release
refusal diagnosis when a version is already taken

examples.description: Adopt the pipeline into the current repository and arm the pre-push hook
Rehearse the whole pipeline without tagging or publishing
Re-check that a published release still matches its build

permissions_systems: Read the local git work tree and its remote configuration
Run the project's configured build commands
Create and push git tags to the configured remote
Create releases and upload assets through the glab or gh CLI
Download a release asset back for verification
Delete a tag and release that this run created, when verification fails
typical_completion_time: one full clean build of the project, plus under a minute for the release steps

data_sources: the GitLab or GitHub release API through glab or gh
required_capabilities: python 3.9+ with the standard library only
glab for GitLab remotes or gh for GitHub remotes, authenticated
readiness_checks: git rev-parse --show-toplevel succeeds in the target directory
the release CLI for the detected provider is on PATH and reports an authenticated session
the configured output directory is git-ignored
exactly one artifact matches artifact.glob after a build

permissions: Create releases and upload assets on the configured remote
Delete the tag and release created by the current run when verification fails
risk.mutation_scope: writes only tags and releases on the configured remote, plus .ci/ inside the repository; it never modifies tracked source files
approval_required: A human installs the pre-push hook explicitly with setup --install-hook
A human reviews and commits .ci/config.json before the first automatic release
verify.rollbackOnFailure may delete the tag and release created by the failing run

affected_structures: .ci/lib/, the vendored runtime copied into the repository
invariants: A published tag never moves to a different commit
The artifact attached to a release is byte-identical to the locally built artifact
HEAD, HEAD tree, tracked-file manifest and work-tree status are identical before and after the build
sources_of_truth: commit identity: git rev-parse HEAD and HEAD^{tree}
artifact version: the produced artifact's file name, cross-checked against its own PE version resource
tag occupancy: the peeled remote tag listing from git ls-remote
invalid_states_prevented: a tag pointing at a commit other than the one that was built
a release whose asset differs from the built artifact
a build that mutates tracked files while a release is being prepared
two different artifacts claiming the same version tag
a release left half-published after a verification failure
state_transitions: no tag -> tag created locally -> tag pushed -> remote tag confirmed -> release created -> asset re-downloaded -> published
any failure after the tag exists -> release deleted, remote tag deleted, local tag deleted -> no tag

authoritative_sources: GitLab Releases API as exposed by glab 1.52 (https://docs.gitlab.com/ee/api/releases/)
GitHub Releases API as exposed by gh 2.96 (https://cli.github.com/manual/gh_release_create)
git plumbing documentation for rev-parse, ls-files, ls-remote and check-ignore
the .ci/config.json schema authored by this skill
relationships: One tag resolves to exactly one commit
One release belongs to exactly one tag
One release carries one or more assets
One artifact is produced by exactly one commit
field_semantics: the tag name is the version string taken from the artifact file name, formatted by the configured template
the artifact SHA-256 is computed over the exact bytes of the build output
the commit SHA identifies the source revision the artifact was built from
invariants: A published tag never moves to a different commit
The asset attached to a release is byte-identical to the locally built artifact
Every remote read happens at verification time and is never cached across a build
freshness_and_pagination: The remote tag listing is re-read after the push and again during read-back
Release asset listings are paged by the provider CLI; the skill requests one named asset and retries with backoff while it becomes available
nullability: An unauthenticated release CLI blocks publishing before the build starts
A missing or ambiguous artifact match blocks the run
An artifact with no PE version resource skips only the embedded cross-check, and says so
readiness_checks: git work tree with a configured remote
the provider CLI is present, authenticated, and exposes the release download operation the read-back depends on
exactly one artifact matches artifact.glob after the build

download a named release asset back
delete a release and its tag during rollback
semantic_recon.freshness_check: contract_health.report() is called before the build; a not-usable report is a safe stop
